provider.name: European Nucleotide Archive
provider.organization_type: nucleotide sequence, read, assembly, sample, study, experiment, analysis, and metadata archive
provider.description: The European Nucleotide Archive is EMBL-EBI's public archive for nucleotide sequence data and associated metadata. It stores studies, samples, experiments, runs, analyses, assemblies, annotated sequences, raw reads, files, taxonomy, and cross-linked accessions, and participates in the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration.
institutional_context: BioSamples and related EMBL-EBI data resources

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting ENA documentation, submission and retrieval guidance, Portal and Browser APIs, Webin workflows, metadata schemas, taxonomy, file formats, downloads, release policy, identifiers, licensing, citation, and institutional context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: ENA, EMBL-EBI, and INSDC remain authoritative for nucleotide records, submission standards, accessions, APIs, file formats, release policy, legal terms, and contact information.

authentication_methods: Anonymous access for public retrieval services
notes: Verify current API paths, result types, fields, limits, pagination, and response formats.
Distinguish public retrieval APIs from authenticated Webin submission interfaces.
Do not store Webin usernames, passwords, FTP credentials, cookies, or tokens in this manifest.
Capture accession syntax, query grammar, field names, file-report semantics, errors, and deprecations.
Capture exact EMBL-EBI and ENA legal wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate metadata, nucleotide sequences, raw reads, assemblies, annotations, sample information, and software.
Preserve embargo, first-public, last-updated, suppression, accession-version, and submitter provenance.
Do not expose confidential or unreleased submissions.
Do not infer rights to human-associated or otherwise sensitive metadata beyond published ENA access controls.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
ENA documentation paths, checklist identifiers, API fields, file formats, and Webin workflows may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every accession, sequence record, sample, study, run, analysis, assembly, taxonomy record, or FTP file when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store Webin usernames, passwords, FTP credentials, API tokens, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Metadata, sequences, raw reads, assemblies, annotations, samples, files, software, and third-party records may carry different rights.
Always preserve accession, accession version, record type, first-public date, last-updated date, file path, checksum, taxonomy ID, release status, and source provenance.
